text: {item} is rich in beta-carotene, which the body turns into vitamin A for healthy eyes and immunity. A little oil in the dish helps it absorb.
source: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements: Vitamin A

text: {item} is one of the best sources of vitamin K, which helps blood clot and keeps bones strong. On warfarin? Keep greens steady from week to week and tell the doctor.
source: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements: Vitamin K

text: {item} is a good source of folate, which the body needs to make healthy red blood cells.
source: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements: Folate

text: {item} brings potassium, which helps balance sodium; diets higher in potassium are linked to lower blood pressure. (Kidney disease? Ask the doctor about potassium first.)
source: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements: Potassium

text: {item} has soluble fibre, which can help lower LDL cholesterol and slows how fast sugar enters the blood.
source: Harvard Health Publishing: Soluble and insoluble fiber

text: {item} adds vitamin C, which helps the body absorb the iron in beans, lentils and greens. A squeeze of lemon on dal does the same.
source: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements: Iron
